recent_posts.title: Fermyon Joins Akamai
recent_posts.summary: Fermyon, a company pioneering WebAssembly-based serverless computing, has been acquired by Akamai Technologies. Founded in 2021, Fermyon built Spin, a developer tool for creating serverless functions with sub-millisecond cold start times, and later partnered with Akamai to launch Fermyon Wasm Functions on Akamai's global edge network. The acquisition enables deeper integration with Akamai's infrastructure, including managed container services and inference cloud capabilities, while Fermyon commits to continuing open source contributions to Spin, SpinKube, Wasmtime, and WASI standards through CNCF and Bytecode Alliance.

recent_posts.title: The MonkCast: WASM and Edge Compute
recent_posts.summary: WebAssembly enables sub-millisecond cold starts for serverless functions, solving the performance penalty that forces teams to keep containers warm in traditional platforms like AWS Lambda. Combined with edge networks that reduce network latency to 7-10ms, this delivers true pay-per-use serverless without sacrificing user experience. Spin, a CNCF project, provides a developer-friendly runtime that mirrors familiar language APIs while enabling hybrid architectures mixing WebAssembly functions with containerized workloads. Real-world applications include edge authentication, geographic content decisions, and ad injection for streaming platforms.

recent_posts.title: Fermyon @ WasmCon + KubeCon NA '25
recent_posts.summary: Fermyon announces their participation at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA 2025 in Atlanta, including booth locations (#422), presentations on serverless WebAssembly and distributed computing, and demos of their Wasm Functions platform. The company is a gold sponsor of WasmCon and silver sponsor of KubeCon, featuring the Spin project at the CNCF Project Pavilion and showcasing AI-powered demos built with Akamai Cloud GPUs. Multiple speaking sessions cover topics like WASIp3, edge computing latency, and globally distributed WebAssembly applications.

recent_posts.title: Build AI Agents with Spin and the OpenAI Agents SDK
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on guide to building AI agents using the OpenAI Agents SDK with Spin framework and TypeScript. The tutorial walks through creating a support agent with FAQ and human handoff capabilities, compiling it to WebAssembly, and deploying it to Fermyon Wasm Functions for globally distributed, serverless execution. Includes complete code examples for defining tools, integrating the agent with an HTTP API, and deploying to production.

recent_posts.title: Thwarting AI Bots with Edge Content Rewriting
recent_posts.summary: Bots now outnumber humans on the web, causing problems like competitive price scraping and unauthorized AI training data collection. A solution combines bot detection services with edge-based WebAssembly functions that act as rewriting proxies. The proxy intercepts bot traffic, uses CSS selectors to identify content sections, and dynamically replaces or redacts sensitive information like pricing. For AI bots, the system can use LLMs to generate summaries instead of exposing original content, allowing sites to maintain search authority while protecting intellectual property. The redacted content is cached at the edge to reduce upstream load.

recent_posts.title: Bringing AI to the Edge with WebAssembly
recent_posts.summary: WebAssembly combined with Kubernetes and GPU acceleration enables ultra-low latency AI inference at the edge. SpinKube allows developers to deploy Wasm applications as Kubernetes-native resources, achieving sub-millisecond cold starts. The Fermyon-Akamai partnership demonstrates how Wasm's sandboxed execution and near-native performance can deliver AI inference services across hundreds of edge locations worldwide, addressing critical challenges in latency, portability, and security for distributed AI workloads.

recent_posts.title: A Bridge over Troubled Water: Sending Azure Alerts to Slack with Spin
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide to building a lightweight Spin application that transforms Azure Monitor alerts into Slack-compatible messages. The solution acts as middleware between Azure's complex JSON alert format and Slack's simple message structure, providing a portable and extensible approach for multi-cloud alert integration. Includes step-by-step deployment instructions and demonstrates monitoring Azure Cosmos DB throttling alerts.

recent_posts.title: Introducing wasi-grpc for Spin
recent_posts.summary: Spin 3.4 introduces outbound HTTP/2 support, enabling WebAssembly components to act as first-class gRPC clients. The new wasi-grpc crate allows Spin applications to directly communicate with gRPC services without requiring sidecars or proxy services. A complete tutorial demonstrates building a Rust-based Spin component that connects to a gRPC service using tonic and the wasi-grpc crate, including setup, configuration, and implementation details.

recent_posts.title: SQLite is Edge-Scale
recent_posts.summary: SQLite emerges as a compelling alternative to traditional distributed databases for edge computing control planes. Despite conventional wisdom favoring complex distributed systems, SQLite offers superior reliability, performance (180k reads/second on modest hardware), and operational simplicity. Combined with tools like Litestream for backup and recovery, SQLite handles the unique challenges of edge deployments including network instability, geographic distribution, and limited infrastructure resources. Real-world implementation at Fermyon demonstrates effective handling of data center outages with minimal impact.

recent_posts.title: Announcing Spin 3.4
recent_posts.summary: Spin 3.4 introduces HTTP/2 support for outgoing requests, enabling seamless integration with gRPC-based backends and improving performance through multiplexed connections. The release adds PostgreSQL connection pooling for better database performance and expands supported data types including UUID, JSONB, and array types. Additionally, Spin templates now include schema directives in spin.toml files for automatic validation and code completion in editors.
